blogs.title: Intrinsic Evidence After Battle: The Eighth Circuit’s Broad View in Felon-in-Possession Cases
blogs.description: The panel reaffirms that prior possession of the same gun is “intrinsic” to prove later possession, sidestepping Rule 404(b). This post unpacks the court’s reliance on Battle, contrasts it with circuits that have narrowed the intrinsic-evidence doctrine, weighs the propensity risks, and offers litigation strategies for charging decisions, motions in limine, and limiting instructions.

blogs.title: Context or Confrontation? Policing the Line on Officer Narrative Testimony
blogs.description: By declining an upfront limiting instruction and leaning on the witness’s in-court testimony to satisfy confrontation concerns, the court blesses the use of out-of-court statements as “context” for police actions. We analyze how this fits with Bennett and Charboneau under Crawford-era doctrine, the risks of backdoor hearsay, and how trial courts can cabin officer narratives without derailing the prosecution.

blogs.title: You Can’t Read From the Report: Authentication, FRE 613, and Impeaching With Police Paperwork
blogs.description: The defense hit a familiar wall: no reading from a police report not authored or adopted by the witness. Using Cumbie, the court underscores authentication requirements for extrinsic impeachment. This post walks through the right foundations (FRE 613(b), 801(d)(1)(A), 803(5), 901), how to use the officer-scribe, and practical templates for clean impeachment.

blogs.title: Harmless Error as Endgame: Why Evidentiary Appeals Keep Failing in the Eighth Circuit
blogs.description: Citing DeMarce and Keys, the panel’s harmless-error and anti-cumulative-error framework again shields a conviction supported by substantial physical and testimonial evidence. We examine the “substantially swayed” standard in practice, how it interacts with preservation and proffers, and what defense counsel must build at trial to avoid post hoc harmlessness.

blogs.title: Stacking Enhancements on Top of ACCA: The Reach of § 2K2.1(b)(6)(B) After Kisor
blogs.description: The court allows a four-level § 2K2.1(b)(6)(B) bump for possession “in connection with another felony,” on top of ACCA and other firearm enhancements, largely via unobjected-to PSR facts and commentary note 14(C). We dissect potential double-counting arguments, the deference owed to Guidelines commentary post-Kisor (and circuit splits like Havis/Nasir/Dupree), and how to preserve ‘in connection with’ challenges for en banc or cert review.

blogs.title: Who Finds ACCA Predicates? The Curious Use of a Jury for Prior Convictions
blogs.description: Although Almendarez-Torres permits judges to find prior convictions, this case used a jury to determine that the defendant had three violent felonies. We explore why the government might choose that path, the interaction with the categorical/modified categorical approach after Wooden and Borden, and whether jury findings reduce appellate risk or invite new complexities.

blogs.title: Presuming Reasonableness, Explaining Less: The Eighth Circuit’s § 3553(a) Minimalism
blogs.description: Relying on Goodhouse, Masood, and Maluoth, the panel affirms a within-Guidelines 292-month sentence with a succinct § 3553(a) discussion. We compare the Eighth Circuit’s deference to other circuits’ expectations for explanation, assess how much is enough to survive appeal, and offer defense strategies for building a record that compels variance or remand.

blogs.title: A Quiet Bench-Slap on Appellate Briefing: Don’t Inflate the Issues
blogs.description: The opinion pointedly notes that appellees should not “unnecessarily expand the issues on appeal.” We situate this admonition within the Eighth Circuit’s norms on precision and restraint in briefing, consider its implications for government practice, and outline best practices for issue framing to preserve credibility with the panel.
